edition.en: G. C. Macaulay’s translation (London, 1890), via Project Gutenberg; his footnote markers are removed.
edition.zh: G. C. 麦考利的英译本（伦敦，1890 年），经古登堡计划；译者的注码已删去。

basis.en: Herodotus wrote in the fifth century BCE. Macaulay’s translation was published in 1890, and he died in 1915.
basis.zh: 希罗多德写作于公元前五世纪。麦考利的译本出版于 1890 年，译者卒于 1915 年。

note.en: These are the first words of the first book of history in the Western tradition, and they say plainly why it was written: so that what people did would not be worn away by time. Herodotus called his work an inquiry, historiē, and the word became the name of the whole subject. Notice that he wants the great works of the ‘Barbarians’, the non-Greeks, remembered as well as those of the Greeks.
note.zh: 这是西方传统中第一部历史著作的开头，它直截了当地说出了写作的理由：不让人们所做的事被时间磨灭。希罗多德把他的著作称为“探究”（historiē），这个词后来成了整门学问的名字。留意他希望被记住的，不只是希腊人的伟业，也包括“异邦人”——非希腊人——的成就。

excerpt.orig: to the end that neither the deeds of men may be forgotten by lapse of time
excerpt.en: to the end that neither the deeds of men may be forgotten by lapse of time
excerpt.zh: 为了不让人们的业绩随着时间流逝而被遗忘

gloss.en: A Greek city on the coast of Caria in Asia Minor, under Persian rule when Herodotus was born; today Bodrum, in Turkey.
gloss.zh: 小亚细亚卡里亚沿岸的希腊城市，希罗多德出生时处于波斯统治之下；即今土耳其的博德鲁姆。

gloss.en: Greek historiē, inquiry or research. Through this book the word came to mean history.
gloss.zh: 希腊文 historiē，意为探究、调查。正是通过这部书，这个词后来有了“历史”的意思。

gloss.en: Greek barbaroi: all who did not speak Greek, Persians and Egyptians among them. In Herodotus the word is not an insult.
gloss.zh: 希腊文 barbaroi，泛指一切不说希腊语的人，包括波斯人和埃及人。在希罗多德笔下，这个词并无贬义。
